title: Protocol to isolate live single cells while retaining spatial information by combining cell photolabeling and FACS
protocol: Collect tumor using scissors and a blade while maintaining tissue integrity.
Trim surrounding fat tissue from the collected tumor.
Place the tumor in one well of a 12-well cell culture plate with prepared medium.
Embed tissue in low melting agarose for sectioning.
Cut the edge of the tumor to generate a flat surface.
Place one drop of Gorilla Glue® into the tissue holder of the specimen tube.
Glue the flat surface of the tumor to the tissue holder.
Place sample holder into the chilling block.
Ensure tissue is located in the center of the sample holder.
Dissolve 0.5 g of agarose in 25 mL of PBS to prepare a 2% agarose solution.
Heat the agarose solution in a microwave until clear.
Cool down the heated agarose solution by washing under cold running water to reach 37°C.
Cut the tip of a 1,000 μL pipette for easy dispensing of dense substances like agarose.
Pour agarose around the tissue into the sample holder carefully.
Avoid bubble formation during pouring of the agarose solution.
Leave approximately 0.2–0.5 cm between the tissue and the edge of the tube to set up compresstome settings before reaching the sample.
Introduce the specimen tube into the chilling block until agarose solidifies.
Slice samples with the compresstome.
Assemble the sample holder into the compresstome following manufacturer instructions.
Place the blade in the correct position.
Secure the buffer tray in place with the screw tightly attached.
Fill the buffer tray with PBS until it covers half of the sample (specimen tube).
Push the tissue advancement plunger until the agarose is seen out of the tube.
Set the machine in single cutting mode.
Adjust speed to 1–3.
Adjust oscillation to 5–6.
Set slice thickness to 300 μm.
Optimize settings for the breast tumors being processed.
Slice through the agarose using manual fast forward to trim tissue-free agarose gel until the tissue appears.
Increase cutting speed during trimming if necessary.
Ensure slices are not thicker than ∼2 mm to maintain even surfaces.
Set continuous mode and higher slice thickness during trimming.
Gradually reduce slice thickness before reaching visible tissue.
Change to single mode once tissue is visible.
Adjust settings according to tissue needs (speed 1–3, oscillation 5–6 typically suitable).
Place sequential slices in pairs in one well of a 12-well plate with medium for storage until image acquisition.
Keep the 12-well plate on ice and covered from light.
Clean the buffer tray, blade, and sample holder after slicing the tumor.
Remove gorilla glue with acetone if needed.
Mount a few drops of medium on the slide before placing the tumor slice.
Set the tumor slice on the slide and carefully extend it using tweezers without damaging the tissue.
Add lubricant eye gel to decrease evaporation and keep slices hydrated during imaging.
Place a coverslip and seal the edges using paraffin or nail polish to fix the sample.
Acquire a tile scan using fast scan rate (short pixel dwell time) and low resolution to generate a full-size image of the whole slice.
Collect green fluorescence from non-photoconverted Kaede using a Zeiss Plan Apochromat 20×/0.8 NA DIC air objective.
Collect red fluorescence from tdTomato-p27k reporter in quiescent cancer cells using the same objective.
Mark positions of interest per slice once a mesoscopic image of the tissue is obtained.
Photoconvert the Kaede protein in tumor slices.
Select positions of interest based on tdTomato-p27k reporter expression in the red channel.
Acquire an image after photoconversion to confirm successful conversion in all selected areas.
Draw a representative region of interest based on tdTomato-p27k reporter expression before and after photoconversion.
Acquire a single confocal image for each marked position in the slice using the same microscope settings as in 5.a.i., except for the pinhole aperture that should be set to maximum.
Draw a defined region of interest (ROI) in the snapshot using the freehand shape tool of the microscope.
Photoconvert the Kaede protein specifically within the ROI.
Scan the whole slice to check the overall photoconversion.
Prepare digestion buffer as specified in the protocol.
Digest the tissue to obtain a single-cell suspension.
Flow sort populations from the single-cell suspension.
Place 500 μL of digestion buffer in a 12-well cell culture plate for each slice.
Put tissue slice into the solution and disrupt tissue with two needles.
Incubate for 15-20 min at 37°C.
Pipette up and down with a 1,000 μL pipette to further disrupt tissue.
Filter digestion with a 100 μm pore size filter, washing the well and the filter with flow buffer (2 mM EDTA, 0.1% BSA in PBS).
Spin down at 800 g for 5 min.
Resuspend digested cells in 500 μL of red blood cell lysis buffer and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash cells with flow buffer.
Spin down at 800 g for 5 min.
Stain single-cell suspension from one slice that has gone through the whole procedure with antibodies, including apoptosis marker Annexin V and viability dye DAPI (BioLegend).
Resuspend stained cells in flow buffer + DAPI (dilution 1:10,000) for sorting.
Set gates using a single-cell suspension from a non-photoconverted slice as a negative control.
Use another single-cell suspension from a photoconverted slice with a large photoconverted area as a positive control.
Check cell viability using the single-cell suspension stained with AnnexinV and DAPI before proceeding further.
Sort enough cells to meet the requirements of your subsequent technique.
Note: In this experimental model, sort 10,000 cells per condition for scRNA-sequencing using the 10× genomics platform.
